title: AR-RC13 regression: substitute action legality re-derived client-side from status; the shipped hooks.can_substitute_referee is never read
detail: The substitute affordance is action legality — the story AC itself frames substitution via the hook ("Given a terminal objected or unreachable row, When the landlord substitutes a referee (can_substitute_referee)"), and the server guards the substitute endpoint on exactly that set. The payload ships hooks.can_substitute_referee and the client ignores it, duplicating the rule in two places (the overflow menu's Unreachable arm and the row-body substitute surface in the Unreachable/Objected branches of row_detail). This is precisely the RC4.2 r1 B1 blocker pattern (client-side is_terminal re-derivation) that the same file's is_terminal was reworked to eliminate — the comment there names the drift rationale (the server's terminal set includes v2-reserved states a client re-implementation misses). The drift risk is already visible in this PR: a taken-over row keeps status='unreachable' (take-over writes only taken_over_at), so the status-derived body surface still renders the "Substitute referee" button on a taken-over row (line 596) while the header menu is correctly suppressed for taken-over rows (view_row: is_taken_over -> row_actions = []) and UX §7.7 says the takeover "replaces the row's action area" — the two status-derived surfaces disagree with each other, and neither consults the hook. The hook surface is the single contract; per the round briefing ("A client-side re-derivation of action legality/status = a blocker [AR-RC13]") this is a blocker.
recommended_fix: Gate the substitute affordance on call.hooks.can_substitute_referee in both the menu (overflow_actions already receives the call, or derive the action list from hooks) and row_detail's Unreachable/Objected branches (render view_substitute_surface only when call.hooks.can_substitute_referee). Keep status only for display copy (state lines, pills), which §8.2 explicitly derives from the enum. If a taken-over row must not offer substitution, that rule belongs in the server hook (compute_hooks_decoded), not in client status cases.

title: Em-dashes in five implementer-authored success toasts (RT em-dash ban; no_em_dash_test does not scan constants)
evidence:
client/src/copy.gleam:874-884:
  pub const refcheck_toast_started: String = "Reference started — the invite goes out now."
  pub const refcheck_toast_re_enabled: String = "Reference re-enabled — it's back in the queue."
  pub const refcheck_toast_taken_over: String = "You're handling this one — automated messages stopped."
  pub const refcheck_toast_corrected: String = "Details saved — the invitation is on its way again."
  pub const refcheck_toast_substituted: String = "Referee substituted — the new invitation is on its way."
These render as landlord-facing toasts via add_toast(..., ToastSuccess) in client.gleam's ApiReturnedRefcheckAction Ok branch. The UX spec fixes no such toast strings (grep of ux-reference-checking-v1-2026-07-29.md for "invite goes out" / "on its way" / "Details saved" / "Reference started" / "re-enabled": no hits) — the file's own comment says "Success toasts (one sentence, brand voice)", i.e. implementer-authored. The RT em-dash pin (client/test/copy_test.gleam:308 no_em_dash_test) iterates only toast(code, ctx) / page(code, ctx) outputs and never sees these constants — the RC4.2 r2 carried warning's gap, and this PR's new copy is exactly where it bites.
detail: Guard 9 + carried warning #2: implementer-authored user-facing strings with em-dashes are findings when this PR adds them (the UX spec's own em-dashes are the verbatim carve-out; these strings are not in the spec). Five of the six new success toasts ship ' — ' where the project's user-facing copy convention (and the CI test) bans it. refcheck_toast_skipped and refcheck_toast_exported are clean. Severity warning: user-facing copy defect, not one of the blocker-graded guards, but it ships past the RT CI check because the pin doesn't scan constants.
recommended_fix: Rephrase without em-dashes, e.g. "Reference started. The invite goes out now.", "Reference re-enabled, back in the queue.", "You're handling this one. Automated messages stopped.", "Details saved. The invitation is on its way again.", "Referee substituted. The new invitation is on its way." — or extend no_em_dash_test to scan the refcheck_* constants so the pin covers the gap.

title: reference_panel.gleam grew 1309 -> 1921 lines this PR (AGENTS.md view-module target <400)
evidence: git show develop:client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam | wc -l -> 1309; wc -l client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam -> 1921 (+612 this PR). The panel now hosts: row rendering, status pills, overflow menu + menu state, start/take-over inline confirms, the §8.3 edit-trio, the correction surface, the substitute surface, the taken-over surface (chips + export), the mini timeline, and the completed/signals views. AGENTS.md: "Target: <200 lines for logic modules, <400 lines for view modules."
detail: The RC4.3 additions (menu, confirms, edit-trio, correction/substitute/taken-over surfaces) all landed in the already-oversized panel module rather than a sub-component. Story RC4.4 (attempt log + full timeline) is planned against this same file, so the trend continues. Functionality is correct and the module keeps a single cohesive owner of the panel, but at ~1900 lines the view is hard to navigate and the module boundary is drifting — the 'row' concept (menu + confirms + edit + takeover) is now several screens' worth of state in one render module.
recommended_fix: When RC4.4 touches the panel, extract the RC4.3 surface blocks into components (e.g. components/refcheck_menu.gleam, refcheck_edit_trio.gleam, refcheck_taken_over.gleam) or a pages/reference_panel/ folder, keeping reference_panel.gleam as a thin orchestrator; no urgent change required for this PR.
